title: Milan: NO RUNNING. Bike + hip abductor block
terrain: indoor bike, zero impact, zero descent
coachNotes: MONDAY EVENING, 24 AUG: THE READ CHANGED AND SO DOES THE WEEK. This morning was tenderness to press only, which is benign. Tonight it is intermittent pin sensations at the lateral knee WHILE WALKING, on the right side. Symptoms during weight-bearing gait are a different category from symptoms on palpation, because walking cycles the knee through the 20-30 degree impingement band under load. That is the prodrome, and it is the thing worth spending three days on. RUNNING IS OFF UNTIL THE WALKING IS CLEAN. Not reduced, off. Early ITBS responds to a short decisive deload; established ITBS does not resolve in 19 days. Spending three flat days now is close to free and it is the highest-value decision available. THE ARITHMETIC THAT MAKES THIS CHEAP: CTL is 43 against a target of 42. There is no fitness left to gain before 12 September. Every session from here is risk management and sharpening, so the cost of cutting is almost zero and the cost of pushing through is the race. BIKE INSTEAD, AND IT IS NOT A CONSOLATION PRIZE: it holds the load so CTL does not fall while removing every impact cycle. SET THE SADDLE 1-2cm HIGHER THAN YOUR NORMAL POSITION and keep cadence 90-100 with moderate resistance. A low saddle and grinding a big gear both drive the knee through more flexion under more force, which is the one way a bike can aggravate a band. If you feel pins on the bike, stop the bike too. STILL DO THE NOBLE TEST, it tells us which problem this is: press hard on the bony bump 2-3cm above the joint line on the outside of the right knee, hold, then slowly straighten and re-bend the knee five times. Sharp familiar pain arriving at about 30 degrees is a positive test. Note the answer, we act on it Thursday. ONE MORE THING, AND DO IT THIS WEEK: book a physiotherapist in Milan. You are alone until Friday, you have a documented March ITBS, and you are 19 days out. Hands on the leg beats anything I can infer from a CSV, and this is the week where it is still cheap to act on what they find. HIP BLOCK, THIS IS THE ACTUAL ITBS INTERVENTION AND IT GOES AHEAD: side-lying hip abduction 3x15 per side, clamshells 3x15 per side, single-leg glute bridges 3x12 per side, side plank with top-leg abduction 3x30s per side, Copenhagen planks 3x20s per side, single-leg calf raises 3x15. Hip abductor weakness with contralateral pelvic drop is the mechanism that lets the band compress the lateral epicondyle, and strengthening it is the one gym intervention with real evidence behind it. OUT THIS WEEK, NO NEGOTIATION: step-downs, split squats, walking lunges, anything that loads a bent knee through 20-40 degrees. Step-downs load precisely the flexion band that is currently symptomatic. Nordics are out too, not because they provoke the band but because there is no reason to add novel soreness in a week we are trying to read a signal through. SELF-CARE: do not foam-roll the IT band itself, you are compressing a structure whose problem is compression. Roll the TFL at the front of the hip, the glutes, and the outer quad above the knee. Ice the lateral knee 10 minutes after training.
